title: How Ultrasound Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how ultrasound works, starting with the book announcement and a banter-heavy intro. They cover sonograms, piezoelectric transducer probes squeezing crystals to produce high-frequency sound, echolocation comparisons with sonar and bats, the history (Karl Dussik's 1942 brain work, Ian Donald's 1950s obstetric use), and the Curie brothers' piezoelectric effect. They describe the machine's components, the transducer array evolution, 2D, 3D, M-mode and Doppler imaging, and clinical uses in obstetrics, cardiology, kidney stones, prostate, and emergency rooms. They discuss safety concerns, including a 2017 study on DNA breakage and heating in animals. The episode closes with a joking walkthrough of an ultrasound exam, future applications (acoustic levitation, drug delivery across the blood-brain barrier, ultrasound liposuction, wound healing), and a listener mail segment plugging a child's podcast.

entities.name: A Child's Perspective of Current Events

segments.title: Book announcement and show open
segments.summary: The hosts promote their upcoming book, Stuff You Should Know: An Incomplete Compendium of Mostly Interesting Things, available for pre-order, then open the show.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck riff on Happy Days episodes, then introduce ultrasound and mention the sonogram article they are working from.

segments.title: What ultrasound is and the crystal principle
segments.summary: Ultrasound is introduced as used for babies and many other things. A transducer probe's crystals are squeezed to produce very high-frequency sound vibrations, and the returning echoes hit the crystals to produce electrical impulses that become images.

segments.title: Echoes, electricity, and history
segments.summary: The hosts describe how echoes bounce back and are converted to electrical impulses and images. They discuss the surprise that crystals are involved, then cover Karl Dussik's 1942 brain tumor search and Ian Donald's 1950s sonogram work.

segments.title: Sonar, echolocation, and image resolution
segments.summary: Ultrasound is compared to military sonar and bat echolocation. The hosts note early bat-based experiments and discuss how higher frequency gives finer resolution but reflects more easily, and how 3D imaging combines frequencies.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief break before returning to the machine.

segments.title: Parts of the ultrasound machine
segments.summary: The hosts walk through the components from an older article: transducer probe types including the internal probe, the CPU and power supply, controls, display, keyboard, disk storage, and printer. They note machines have changed little beyond getting smaller and more powerful.

segments.title: Transducer arrays and the piezoelectric effect
segments.summary: The hosts explain how early probes used a single crystal and how arrays of crystals improved resolution. They credit Pierre and Jacques Curie with discovering the piezoelectric effect in the 1880s and discuss how echo intensity maps tissue density.

segments.title: 2D, 3D, M-mode, and Doppler imaging
segments.summary: The hosts describe 2D snapshots, 3D imaging from crystal arrays, M-mode for motion, and Doppler ultrasound for blood flow, comparing Doppler color maps to weather radar.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief break before the clinical uses discussion.

segments.title: Clinical uses of ultrasound
segments.summary: Obstetric uses include checking size, position, placenta, number of fetuses, ectopic pregnancy, and amniotic fluid, plus guiding amniotic sampling. Other uses include cardiology valve checks, kidney stones, prostate lumps, and emergency room triage.

segments.title: Ultrasound safety
segments.summary: The hosts say ultrasound is generally considered safe with no radiation, though heat and bubble formation are concerns. They mention a 2017 study finding DNA strand breaks and animal heating from some continuous-wave and rapid pulsed ultrasound.

segments.title: Joking exam walkthrough and future applications
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read a tongue-in-cheek Franz Kafka guide to getting an ultrasound, then discuss acoustic levitation, ultrasound-boosted chemotherapy across the blood-brain barrier, ultrasound liposuction, and wound healing.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener mail from eleven-year-old Dagan Hofeld promotes his podcast A Child's Perspective of Current Events. The hosts give a plug and sign off.
